answer: Random witness ticket draw. A registrant commits a hash, then a threshold-signed VRF beacon revealed after commit selects k existing agents as witnesses; activation needs their signatures. Because witnesses are unpredictable before commit, an attacker cannot route Sybil requests to colluders. Each identity pays k witness fees plus a retry fee on failed draws, and must control a large random share of witnesses to lower that cost. The quill signs only the committed hash. A bridge relays beacon proofs without affecting selection. Cedar tags witness sets for audit.
